cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles in Babylon, is seeing a vision of a new temple (Ezek 1:1-3; 40:2). A man who looks like bronze has been walking him through it, gate by gate (Ezek 40:3). Now the Lord GOD speaks, starting with the gate of the inner court that faces east.

cards.question: The Lord GOD says the inner court's east gate stays shut during the six days of work. So when does it open?

answers.text: On the Sabbath and the New Moon
On Passover and the Day of Atonement
At the start of every harvest

cards.text: In comes the prince, the leader this vision keeps mentioning (Ezek 44:3). He enters from outside through the gateway's portico and stands by the gatepost.

cards.question: The prince stands by the gatepost while the ___ sacrifice his burnt offerings and peace offerings.
Before the prince departs, what does he do at the threshold of the gate?
On the Sabbath, once the prince departs, the east gate gets shut right away.
That gate stays open until evening. On Sabbaths and New Moons, the ___ of the land also bow in worship before the LORD at the entrance to that gateway.

cards.text: Next comes the offering list: six lambs and a ram on the Sabbath, and on the New Moon a young bull too, all without blemish. Grain and oil go with them, and with the lambs the prince gives as much as he is able, which is EXACTLY how I measure chocolate chips.

When the prince goes in through the gateway's portico, he goes out the same way. But at the appointed feasts, the people of the land get a different rule, made for a big crowd that has to keep moving.

cards.question: At the appointed feasts, a worshiper comes in by the north gate. Which gate does he leave by?

cards.text: Nobody goes back out the gate he came in by: in north, out south, in south, out north. It's a one-way hallway, and baker, I have BEEN the guy walking against the whole crowd, mustache first, apologizing to everybody.

cards.question: At the appointed feasts, the prince goes in with the people and leaves when they leave.

cards.text: At the festivals and appointed feasts, the grain and oil offerings follow the same pattern as the New Moon. Same recipe, different day, friend, and that is my FAVORITE kind of recipe.
Now say the prince brings a freewill offering to the LORD, a burnt offering or a peace offering. He offers it just as he does on the Sabbath, and once he goes out, the gate is closed behind him.

cards.question: For the prince's freewill offering, which gate gets opened for him?

cards.text: Then comes a permanent rule for every single morning: an unblemished year-old lamb as a burnt offering to the LORD, with a grain offering of fine flour moistened with oil. Regular as an alarm clock, friend, and unlike me and MY alarm clock, nobody hits snooze on this one.
Now the Lord GOD talks about the prince's land. If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons as an inheritance, it belongs to his descendants as their property.

cards.question: But say the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants instead. What happens to it in the year of freedom?

answers.text: It goes back to the prince
It passes to the servant's sons

cards.text: Back to the prince it goes. His inheritance belongs only to his sons.

cards.question: The prince may take the people's land by evicting them, so he can give it to his sons.
The prince has to give his sons an inheritance from his own property. What does the Lord GOD say this rule is for?

answers.text: So none of His people are displaced from their property
So the prince's sons never argue over who gets the land
So the land around the temple can keep growing larger

cards.text: Then the man guiding Ezekiel brings him through a side entrance into the holy chambers facing north, the ones that belonged to the priests. There, at the far western end, he shows him a place.

cards.question: The man shows Ezekiel a place at the far western end of the priests' holy chambers. What is that place for?

cards.text: The priests boil the guilt offering and the sin offering here, and they BAKE the grain offering. Baker, I heard that word and my mustache shot straight up like somebody finally called my number at the DMV.

cards.question: The priests cook these offerings back in this place so they don't bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.

cards.text: Then the man brings Ezekiel into the outer court and leads him around to its four corners. In every corner, Ezekiel sees a separate court.

cards.question: The enclosed courts in the four corners of the outer court are each a different size.

cards.text: All four match: forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. Baker, I have NEVER once made four cookies the same size, because one always comes out HUGE and one looks like it just gave up.

cards.question: Around the inside of each corner court runs a row of masonry, with ___ built at the base of the walls on all sides.
The man tells Ezekiel these are kitchens where those who minister at the temple will cook the sacrifices offered by the ___.

cards.text: And that's where I'll set the timer for now, friend, because this vision is NOT finished yet.
